predicted_errors.error_location: Section II, paragraph beginning "For the all-one codeword, the short-term spectrum looks very similar..."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that, because GSM uses differential precoding, a sequence of 148 repeated '1'-bits is converted into 'a sequence of at least 147 0-symbols' before modulation, producing a near-identical (upward) frequency shift as the all-zero codeword, with the waveform merely phase-shifted by π. However, the paper's own premise requires that feeding an all-zero bit sequence (the real GSM frequency-correction burst) directly produces a constant symbol stream (continuous upward tone) without complication — this is only possible under the standard GSM differential (NRZI-style) encoding convention where a '0' input bit causes NO toggle of the encoded symbol (and a '1' input causes a toggle), which is also the well-established real-world convention (the FCB's 142 fixed zero bits are known to produce a pure, continuous tone precisely because '0' does not toggle the differentially-encoded symbol). Under this necessary convention, however, a sequence of 148 '1' bits would toggle the encoded symbol at every step, producing an ALTERNATING 0,1,0,1,... symbol sequence rather than the claimed near-constant run of '147 0-symbols'. The same issue recurs later for the R_l codewords {1010...,0101...}, which are likewise claimed to differentially precode into 'an all-one sequence of at least 147 symbols' — but an alternating raw bit pattern passed through the same (necessarily fixed) differential encoding convention yields a period-4 (not constant) output. The two claims about how differential precoding transforms these bit patterns are mutually inconsistent with any single, fixed differential encoding rule, and also inconsistent with the well-documented real-world behavior of the GSM frequency correction burst.

The abstract states: 'Although it is a frequency modulation, its transmit signal shows close to rectangular spectral shape.' This is a strong claim of near-ideal (brick-wall-like) spectral confinement, but nowhere in the body of the paper is such a result demonstrated or quantified. Instead, the body repeatedly discusses asymmetric spectra with residual sidelobes (e.g., 'The modified spectrum has a raised carrier frequency with reduced sidelobes... The spectrum is asymmetric', and discussion of sidelobes contributing to inter-carrier interference or out-of-band radiation in Figs. 1-3). The evidence presented supports improved/narrower spectral confinement relative to unmodified CPFSK, not an actual close-to-rectangular spectral shape, making the abstract's characterization an overstatement relative to the supporting evidence.
